QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_17

question.text: As the Manager of a newly launched Cat III AIF, your checklist of general obligations under Regulation 20 must include appointing a CUSTODIAN. This requirement applies:

answer.text: Only if fund corpus exceeds INR 500 crore
Only if the fund holds listed securities, not unlisted
For all AIFs — the Sponsor or Investment Manager shall appoint a SEBI-registered custodian for safekeeping of securities/goods
Only for Cat III AIFs; Cat I and II are exempt

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 20(11A) mandates that every AIF appoint a SEBI-registered custodian for safekeeping of securities and goods. There is no corpus threshold, listed/unlisted carve-out, or category exemption. The custodian is appointed by the Sponsor or Investment Manager. The Trap: Corpus and listed-only carve-outs are pre-amendment historical positions that are no longer applicable. Cat-III-only is a popular distractor based on leverage concerns — but Cat I and II also need custodians. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B touch this lightly. XIX-C expects knowledge of the custodian's operational role including trade settlement, corporate-action handling, and segregated scheme accounts. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate the custodian SLA before first close — once LP capital is drawn, leverage to reduce basis-point fees evaporates. Also insist on per-scheme segregation in writing; omnibus accounts create ring-fencing issues if one scheme faces an investor claim.
